known_facts_book1: A poor charcoal-burner of Regos who lives with his wife and daughter in a log cabin more than a mile off the beaten path, to avoid the King's lawless soldiers.
Is left alone by the wild beasts of the forest, who have come to regard him as one of its natural dwellers because he never hunts them.
Finds one of Inga's shoes lying by the palace wall and the other on a dust-heap round the corner, and pockets both as a present for his daughter Zella.

Kills Choggenmugger, the Great Beast that had eaten every dragon, serpent and crocodile in Regos, chopping it into small pieces with his axe — and believes it was his own strength, never knowing the pearls were in his coat pocket.
Refuses on his bended knees to be made King of the Twin Islands, saying the warriors would murder him within a month.
Refuses also to be made rich, arguing that he has been safe for years precisely because he owned nothing anyone could envy.
Says the poor and humble man who lives unnoticed escapes the troubles of the rich and famous and is the only one who can appreciate the joy of living — advice the whole council profits by.
Directs the men of Pingaree in rebuilding their homes, and asks only to move his family there.
Is made general manager of the buildings and the pearl fisheries, and at the end is made Lord High Chamberlain of Pingaree by King Kitticut.

known_relations_book1.Zella: His daughter, to whom he gives the magic shoes without knowing what they are.
known_relations_book1.Inga: The Prince who offers him a crown and riches, both of which he refuses.
known_relations_book1.King Kitticut: The King who finally makes him Lord High Chamberlain.
known_relations_book1.Choggenmugger: The Great Beast he destroys by accident of the pearls.

not_in_this_book: Nikobob knows about the Magic Pearls

known_facts_book1: The little daughter of Nikobob the charcoal-burner and his wife, who had never owned shoes before her father brought her Inga's pair.
Gathers wild honey with her mother from hollow trees, and carries a pail of it once a year to Queen Cor, who is fond of it.
Sets out for Coregos with two pails instead of one, wearing the red pointed shoes, and so carries both Magic Pearls across Regos without knowing it.
Snaps a barrier of branches like dried twigs, lifts a fallen log six men could not move, and throws a charging wild boar by one ear — and is worried by a strength she did not know she had.
Stands unharmed in a swarm of angry bees, and afterwards keeps working while her mother runs away.
Meets Inga at the back door of Queen Cor's palace and gives up the shoes willingly in exchange for his new red leather ones, never knowing what she has traded.
Is comforted by Inga when she cannot sell her honey, and is paid for it out of Queen Cor's abandoned purse by Rinkitink.
Cooks the party's meals aboard the boat and in Queen Cor's palace, being a good little cook who often helped her mother.
Moves with her parents to Pingaree, where Inga finds her living happily in the cottage her father built near the King's palace.

known_relations_book1.Nikobob: Her father, who brings her the shoes from Regos.
known_relations_book1.Inga: The Prince who trades her his own shoes for the magic pair.
known_relations_book1.Queen Cor: The Queen she brings honey to each year and never actually sells it to.
known_relations_book1.Rinkitink: Who pays her several gold pieces for the honey.

not_in_this_book: Zella knows about the Magic Pearls
Zella sells her honey to Queen Cor
Zella refuses to give up the shoes
